significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: the linearly decoded "harmfulness verdict" at the "</think> boundary" predicts labeled harmfulness better than visible chain-of-thought and forecasts whether answer generation will honor or reverse that state, with a form-(ii) causal addition from re-asserting the verdict to suppress overrides. This supplies both a behavioral phenomenon—dissociations labeled "faked refusals" and "silent overrides"—and a proposed mechanism involving answer-phase decay or reversal, although interpreting a harmful-request verdict plus refusal as a "faked refusal" is conceptually weaker than showing unsafe response intent. Turpin et al. (2023) and Lanham et al. (2023) make faithfulness of chain-of-thought a real monitoring concern, while Arditi et al. (2024) shows that residual-stream refusal features can causally control behavior; therefore, fixing the temporal relation among a boundary verdict, visible reasoning, and later output would constrain where safety decisions are formed and lost, whereas a negative result would rule out this boundary state as a privileged monitor rather than merely failing to find an arbitrary feature. Verified-true and verified-false are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: generic mechanistic LLM safety would not itself imply the claim-specific predictive ordering, two-way dissociation, and answer-phase reversal trajectory.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is a "threshold detector on the </think> verdict projection," supplemented by an intervention that "re-asserts the latent verdict at the answer boundary"; the detector is ex ante because it is available before answer generation and can leave time to gate or modify the response. The asserted coupling—boundary verdict outperforming CoT text and predicting later override—can remain meaningful after per-model re-extraction, although the exact direction and threshold are not themselves claimed to transfer unchanged. Scope extends across open reasoning-model families and attack classes with explicit thinking boundaries, but the claim expressly leaves frontier and hidden-CoT systems unestablished; downstream users could include deployment auditors and safety-gating practitioners, not only researchers analyzing the same failures. The topic-substitution check supports an above-median score because the generic safety-interpretability topic supplies neither this early-warning boundary signal nor its pre-output action window.
